> **Renamed in 4.0.0: `dsh-purge` → `Xsdsh-purge`.** Package name, plugin name, install dirs, module
specifiers, HTTP routes (`/Xsdsh-purge/*`), CSS prefixes, localStorage keys, the data dir and the b
ackup suffix all changed. **Existing installs migrate themselves**: already-injected host markers ar
e rewritten on the next *Clean*, legacy `.dshpurge.bak` backups still restore, `$DSH_HOME/dsh-purge`
moves to `$DSH_HOME/Xsdsh-purge` on first boot, and the wallpaper / glass settings carry over from
the old localStorage keys.
> **Updates paused.** The author has no steady income for now because of work. Maintenance is on hol
d: no new releases, issues / PRs are not taken, and new dsh versions are not guaranteed. The repo st
ays usable; see Sponsor below. When maintenance resumes, this README will say so.
> **Official Web and the official desktop app are both supported.** Official `dsh web` uses profile
`web`. The official desktop EXE (DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.5**) uses profile `desktop`. Install an
d Apply them separately. This release pins `engines.dsh` to **0.2.1-rc.5** exactly; other dsh builds
(including the 0.2.1-rc.2 web host) need a matching plugin build. Community Desktop is not maintain

ed.
>
> Adding the plugin to a profile does not patch the host. Click **Xsdsh-purge** beside the ses
sion title → **Clean** → **Apply**. A successful Apply restarts; an unfinished Apply does not. After

the restart, start a new chat — that is when the inject enters the session.

## What this is
**Xsdsh-purge** is a cybersecurity red-team plugin for the official DeepSeek Harness already install
ed on your machine. Official **Web** (`dsh web`) and the official **desktop EXE** are both supported
. Install and Apply them separately.
Harness does more than forward a prompt. It rewrites prompts, approval gates, sandbox policy, and se
ssion migration at runtime. Asking only “will the model answer” treats a host-layer block as a model
refusal. This plugin separates those two layers on your own install, for controlled evaluation and
for seeing which default policy is too tight.
| You get | What it does |
| **Xsdsh-purge dock** | A button beside the session title opens the right dock. Three pages: Clean,

Rewrite and Drill |
| **Clean** | Grouped patch status, Apply / Restore / Uninstall, prompt editor,

multiple rule sets |
| **Rewrite** | Turns a rough request into one precise, actionable prompt. Use

s the host's current model — no extra endpoint or API key |
| **Drill** | Built into the stable rele
ase: assets, skills, and the local environment. It **assumes you control every target you submit and
already hold the authorization** — it never asks about ownership, written authorization, or SRC sco

pe |
| **Host policy** | Default copy, permission policy, and tool limits. Official capabilities sta

y. No second invented identity |
| **On start** | Checks and reapplies. After npm overwrites `node_m
odules`, you do not hand-edit files |
No hardcoded drive letters. It looks at `$DSH_HOME`, `.dsh` next to the dsh launcher, then `~/.dsh`.
It does not patch the Harness source tree. **Apply** on the **Clean** page of **Xsdsh-purge** is wh
at writes the changes. Identity comes from the encrypted prompt shipped in the plugin, the text the
prompt box shows by default. The host prompt file is not read.
It only touches the official `@deepseek-ai` packages and local config on the user's machine. It is n
ot a public scanner and not an attack kit for third-party sites. The repo does not ship malware, una
uthorized-exploit scripts, or payloads aimed at the public internet.
